keyPoints: HistoryApiStorage is the only storage backend actually used by any section today — the GitHub- and Blob-Storage-backed classes (github_storage.py, blob_storage.py) are dead code, referenced only by their own tests
Private sections enforce per-item read access: only the item's author can view it; wrong-owner requests return 404 instead of 403
Private sections require authentication for all operations, including reads, aligning with ownership-based visibility rules
Legacy items without stamped author_email remain accessible to any allowlisted writer, ensuring backward compatibility
HistoryApiStorage backend enables version-history operations, including optimistic concurrency checks for create, update, and delete
Application Insights integration enables telemetry for HTTP request metrics like call volume, latency, and error rates
architecture.overview: Azure Functions v2 app (Python) deployed to a Consumption plan. Each HTTP trigger handles one REST operation. Content is organized into named sections, each with its own schema and visibility rules. Both current sections — writing and diary — use HistoryApiStorage exclusively: every get/list/create/update/delete call is an HTTP request to [[posts-api|history-api]], which is now the sole storage backend, not an optional add-on. The repo also still contains GitHub- and Blob-Storage-backed storage classes from before the history-api migration; neither is wired into any current section and both are exercised only by their own unit tests. Auth uses google-auth to validate Google ID tokens server-side; no session state is maintained. Private sections enforce authentication and ownership checks for all operations, including reads. Application Insights integration provides telemetry for HTTP request metrics, enabling detailed usage analysis.

dataFlow.label: Ownership / allowlist check
sublines: POST: email must be in ALLOWED_WRITERS
PUT/DELETE: requester must match author_email (or be in allowlist for legacy items)
Private sections require allowlist membership for all operations, including reads
Private-section reads: requester must match author_email; wrong-owner requests return 404

dataFlow.label: Version-history operations
sublines: GET /versions: mirrors get_item visibility rules (private sections require auth + allowlist + author match)
GET /versions/{version_id}: retrieves a specific version of an item
GET /versions/{v1}/diff/{v2}: computes a diff between two versions of an item

dataFlow.label: Telemetry data collection
sublines: Application Insights captures HTTP request metrics automatically for all endpoints
Metrics include call volume, latency, error rates, and usage patterns by time of day

description: A serverless write API for quixotry.me's content sections. Both current sections (writing, diary) store their content as history-api documents — every read and write is an HTTP call to history-api, not a GitHub commit. Application Insights integration enables telemetry for HTTP request metrics like call volume, latency, and error rates.
features: Both "writing" and "diary" sections are private (writing was made private after this feature list was first written) and both are fully backed by history-api, not GitHub
Restrict private-section reads to the item's own author; other authors' entries are excluded
Private sections return 404 for wrong-owner requests, avoiding confirmation of item existence
Private sections require authentication for all operations, including reads
Legacy item support: items without author_email remain visible to any allowlisted writer
Version-history support: list, retrieve, and diff versions of content items via [[posts-api|history-api]]
Application Insights integration: HTTP request telemetry for metrics like call volume, latency, and error rates
role: Manages content sections (writing, diary), both fully backed by history-api
summary: Azure Functions (Python) API that manages content sections — currently writing and diary, both private and both fully backed by history-api (not GitHub). Authentication is handled via Google ID tokens; content ownership is enforced per-creator, with an allowlist controlling who can write. Application Insights provides telemetry for HTTP request metrics, enabling detailed usage analysis.
